title: What If a Lake Exploded With Gas? One Did in 1986

scenes.text: What if a quiet lake suddenly breathed out a deadly cloud? In 1986, one did.
Lake Nyos in Cameroon is 208 meters deep. For decades, volcanic carbon dioxide seeped in and stayed trapped in its bottom water.
On August 21, 1986, something disturbed it. About a cubic kilometer of gas burst out and rolled downhill at up to 70 kilometers an hour.
Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, so it hugged the valleys. People were found dead up to 25 kilometers away.
By morning, 1,746 people and about 3,500 livestock were dead. A landslide is the likely trigger.
Since 2001, pipes have let the gas out slowly. By 2012, the lake held about 40 percent less carbon dioxide.

description:
What if a lake suddenly released a cloud of deadly gas? In 1986, Lake Nyos in Cameroon did.
About a cubic kilometer of carbon dioxide killed 1,746 people up to 25 kilometers away. Pipes now let the gas out safely.
